Centre questions Karnataka’s Ethanol testing process. So what is the prescribed procedure

The Centre has found fault with Karnataka’s sampling and testing methods used to claim that petrol contained 26-31 percent ethanol. ThePrint explains how ethanol content is supposed to be tested.

Udit Bubna

10 November, 2026 09:30 am IST

New Delhi: India’s E20 programme requires oil marketing companies to ensure that petrol supplied to consumers meets prescribed ethanol-blending and fuel-quality standards, with ethanol content maintained within the 19–21 percent range. But verifying whether the fuel meets these standards depends not just on the laboratory conducting the test, but also on how samples are collected, handled and analysed.

Oil marketing companies (OMCs) allege that Karnataka’s October exercise deviated from the prescribed procedure. They say samples were collected without their representatives present and that they have not received the retained samples, outlet-wise details or laboratory reports.

These procedures have come under scrutiny following Karnataka’s Congress government claiming that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contained 26–31 percent ethanol, significantly above the prescribed E20 limit of 20 percent ethanol.

Show Full Article

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) and the three public sector OMCs—Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL)—have questioned both the sampling process and the laboratory methods used in Karnataka’s October 2026 exercise.

The latest controversy comes amid wider concerns over E20 petrol. In July, the policy faced criticism over possible mileage losses, particularly in older vehicles. The Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) also flagged fuel-quality concerns, including chloride contamination and moisture, in a communication to the petroleum ministry. It later withdrew the communication, saying some figures needed further authentication.

EXPOSED: The document the Government tried hard to erase.

On July 28, 2026, SIAM officially warned the Union Govt that Excessive chloride in E20 petrol is actively damaging your vehicles.

Instead of protecting your hard earned money & your vehicles the govt went after news… pic.twitter.com/UEvExxS2jT

— Tehseen Poonawalla Official 🇮🇳 (@tehseenp) August 11, 2026

While the July debate centred on mileage and vehicle compatibility, the Karnataka controversy concerns whether petrol contained more ethanol than permitted. The process requires petrol samples to be collected and analysed in accordance with prescribed procedures.

According to Centre, these procedures are laid down under the Motor Spirit and High-Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, and the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024.

Under these rules, six one-litre samples must be collected from a petrol outlet. Two are handed to the dealer against acknowledgement, two are retained by the oil company or inspecting department, and the remaining two are sent to a laboratory specified under the control order.

Sample labels must be jointly signed, and test results communicated to the dealer and oil company within the prescribed timeframe. This allows all parties to verify the findings and seek retesting if they disagree.

The OMCs have also questioned the use of certificates from a third-party laboratory instead of a laboratory specified under the control order. The OMCs say the absence of samples and documentation has prevented them and the dealers from independently verifying the results or seeking a retest.

What methods should laboratories use? Even if samples are collected correctly, laboratories must follow prescribed technical standards to establish their ethanol content.

The relevant specification is identified under IS 17021:2018, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standard for ethanol-blended motor gasoline. The amendment, issued in August 2025, prescribes three methods for measuring ethanol content in E20 petrol.

The first is Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), which uses infrared light to identify and measure the concentration of substances in a fuel sample.

The second is water extraction method. Since ethanol mixes readily with water while petrol does not, this method uses water to separate ethanol from petrol before measuring its content through the prescribed procedure.

The third is Gas Chromatography, a laboratory technique that separates the different chemical components of a fuel sample so their individual quantities can be measured. It must follow the prescribed ASTM D4815 or D6839 standards. ASTM International is an organisation that develops standardised testing methods for materials and products.

Gas Chromatography also has specific requirements. The sample must first be diluted in equal proportions with oxygenate-free petrol, meaning petrol without ethanol or other oxygen-containing blending components. The result must then be corrected using an E10 certified reference material—a sample with a known composition used to check the accuracy of laboratory measurements.

The Centre says Karnataka’s laboratory certificates only mention that ethanol was measured using Gas Chromatography. They do not specify which ASTM standard was followed, whether the required dilution was carried out or which reference material was used.

Without these details, the reported ethanol levels of 26–31 percent cannot be independently validated against IS 17021, the Centre argues.

Why the Centre questioned the results The Ministry has questioned the density readings in Karnataka’s certificates. Since ethanol is denser than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the fuel’s overall density.

Karnataka’s certificates recorded densities of 0.742–0.749 grams per cubic centimetre for samples reportedly containing 26-31 percent ethanol. In comparison, OMC tests of E20 samples recorded densities of 0.752–0.760 grams per cubic centimetre. The Centre says this difference warrants further examination through prescribed testing and comparison with appropriate reference samples.

The OMCs have also cited their nationwide quality-monitoring exercise conducted with the Centre for High Technology (CHT), under Petroleum Ministry. Of 893 samples collected from depots and retail outlets across 27 states and Union Territories, all were found to contain ethanol within the prescribed range of 19-21 percent.

This included 56 samples from Karnataka, covering all three OMCs and different locations. Their ethanol content ranged between 19 and 20 percent, averaging 19.30 percent.

The OMCs have sought Karnataka’s sampling records, laboratory reports and access to the samples. They have proposed joint testing at an authorised laboratory with representatives of both sides to establish whether the reported ethanol levels are accurate and meet the prescribed testing standards.

(Edited by Viny Mishra)

By Steve Gorman Nov 9 (Reuters) – A federal judge in Florida has ordered a psychiatric evaluation for Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain’s Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, to determine if he is mentally fit to answer to charges accusing him of being a child sex predator.

US Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin in Tampa wrote in a two-page order on Friday that the initial court appearance of Prince Harry’s 82-year-old father-in-law, including a “lack of recall,” raised questions in her mind as to whether he was competent to face prosecution.

Thomas Markle was arrested on Friday on a single federal count of possessing child sexual abuse material, including two explicit photographs of himself posed with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress.

Show Full Article

One of the photos showed a naked girl in a room that appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines, where Markle previously resided for some time.

According to an FBI affidavit filed in court as part of the criminal complaint lodged against Markle, federal agents seized the material in question, part of a cache of slides, film negatives and books, from storage units Markle had rented in Los Angeles since 2008.

Commenting on the case on Friday, FBI Director Kash Patel said Markle “targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions.”

Markle was most recently residing in Lakeland, Florida, where according to the Daily Mail he was a nursing home patient.

No plea was entered during Friday’s hearing, and the judge permitted Markle to be released from custody on personal recognizance on condition that he submit to home detention and electronic monitoring.

The Tampa-based federal public defender assigned to represent Markle, Mary Claire Wolf, did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

In a court order after the hearing, Griffin said she found “reasonable cause to believe” that Markle may “suffer from a mental disease or defect rendering him mentally incompetent to the extent that he is unable to understand the nature and consequences of the proceedings against him or to assist properly in his defense.”

Griffin said she based her findings on unspecified information provided about his health condition, his “advanced age, and lack of recall.”

The judge also appointed Dr Amie Gerodimos, a forensic psychiatrist, to conduct an independent psychiatric exam of Markle and to render a diagnosis of his condition with a finding on his mental fitness to stand trial.

Griffin set a November 20 deadline for Gerodimos to report back to the court.

(Reporting by Steve Gorman in Los Angeles; Editing by Cynthia Osterman)

By Jason Lange WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) – President Donald Trump’s approval rating held near the lowest level of his political career, depressed by national concerns over rising prices that tanked his Republican Party in last week’s midterm elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.

Some 32% of Americans approve of Trump’s performance in the White House, unchanged from two prior Reuters/Ipsos polls conducted between late October and early November. It was one percentage point higher than his 31% rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll in mid-October, the lowest of his career in politics.

Trump’s Republican Party suffered a staggering defeat in the November 3 midterm elections, losing control of both chambers of the US Congress. With some races still undecided, Democrats scored their biggest victory in the House of Representatives since at least 2008 while flipping Senate seats in traditionally conservative states including Kansas, South Carolina and Texas.

Show Full Article

The poll showed just 21% of Americans giving Trump a thumbs-up on his management of the cost of living. The war launched by the president on Iran in February has raised fuel prices sharply and weighed on household finances. Trump’s low rating on the issue has also hurt his allies in Congress.

Trump’s approval rating on immigration policy, at 38%, remains considerably higher than the 25% rating Americans give his economic stewardship.

Some 81% of Republicans in the poll supported Trump’s immigration approach, compared with 50% who did so on the cost of living. Trump has aggressively ramped up deportations of immigrants since he returned to the White House in January 2025 and last week promoted Stephen Miller, a key architect of those policies, to be the new White House chief of staff.

The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online nationwide November 6 to 9, gathered responses from 1,705 US adults and had a margin of error of about 2 percentage points.

(Reporting by Jason Lange; editing by Scott Malone and Cynthia Osterman)
